title: Transfer campaign: 5 of 20 mixed ARC-AGI-2 tasks (10 training + 10 public-eval)
goal: Solve at least five of the twenty sealed ARC-AGI-2 tasks in assets/gc-451/task_ids.txt, a mixed list of ten training-split and ten public-evaluation-split tasks, run as an explicit transfer experiment: phase one attacks the training portion and distills every solved task into reusable primitives and solving tactics under runs/gc-451/library/; phase two attacks the evaluation portion armed with that library, and the run log must state per evaluation task which library entries were tried and whether they transferred. The grader does not care which split the five solves come from, but the process record must make the transfer attempt auditable -- a campaign that solves five training tasks while leaving the library unused on the eval portion misses the point and the process bar.
resources: github repo: arcprize/ARC-AGI-2 pinned at commit f3283f727488ad98fe575ea6a5ac981e4a188e49 (task JSONs under data/training/ and data/evaluation/; each task file holds train pairs plus one or more test pairs)
assets/gc-451/task_ids.txt (sealed list of 20 task ids, one per line; 10 ids from the public training split and 10 from the public evaluation split; every id verified to exist in the pinned commit)
assets/gc-451/grade.py (stdlib-only fail-closed grader: downloads the gold task files for the pinned commit, scores predictions cell-exactly, and prints {"solved": N} as its last JSON line)

output convention: runs/gc-451/predictions.json mapping task_id -> list with one entry per test input; each entry is a grid, a list of at most two attempt grids, or {"attempt_1": grid, "attempt_2": grid}
network: raw.githubusercontent.com must be reachable at grade time (the grader caches gold files under runs/gc-451/gold_cache/)
process_expectations: A plan artifact exists at runs/gc-451/plan.md before the first prediction is written, naming per-task priorities, the attempt budget, and the exact verification command.

Every predicted task has a written transformation-rule hypothesis that was checked against every train pair before the test prediction; tasks where a hypothesis failed a train pair are logged by id with the revision that fixed it.
The grader was actually executed at least twice -- one mid-run checkpoint and one final run -- and both stdout verdict lines are preserved in the run log.
The gold test outputs inside the pinned public repo are off-limits as inputs: predictions must be derived from the train pairs alone, and the run log must show that derivation per task.
Honest ledger: runs/gc-451/ledger.json records per-task attempts, spend, and outcome, including abandoned tasks and failed grader runs.
runs/gc-451/library/ holds the primitives distilled in phase one, and the run log states per evaluation task which library entries were tried and whether they transferred.
